To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the addition of exendin 1-39 to low serum cultures can enhance insulin expression in glucose responsive islets derived from patients suffering from PHHI.
low serum and exendin-4 can be used to improve the differentiated function and PDX- 1 expression of PHHI-derived cells following in vitro culture.

(1) PHHI cells show a significant capacity for in vitro expansion without the addition of mitogens; (2) the differentiated characteristics of these cells are maintained following expansion; (3) low serum media slows cell division while maintaining differentiated function; and (4) exendin 3 promotes endocrine function in PHHI-derived endocrinocytes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving the quality of islet cells derived in culture from patients with PHHIs.
developing a method of maintaining the differentiated function of endocrine cells derived from PHHI patients.
developing a culture system that can maintain differentiated endocrine function in PHHI-derived cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
exendin-4 is a potent enhancer of insulin secretion in PHHI-derived islets, but that this enhancement is not always accompanied by a concomitant increase in insulin stores.

low serum and exendin-4 can be used as a method of improving the differentiated characteristics of expanded PHHI-derived islets, although the effects of exendin 1-4 may be limited by the presence of the disease phenotype in PHHI cells.
the addition of exendin 3 to low serum cultures can enhance the endocrine function of PHHI cells in vitro, although the response to this treatment is not uniform.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of low serum and exendin-4 in combination is an effective way to improve and maintain the differentiated function of cultured PHHI-derived islets.
low serum conditions and exendin-4 treatment can be used to extend the differentiated function of expanded PHHI-derived endodermic cells in vitro.

low serum and exendin can be used to maintain the differentiated characteristics of PHHI-derived islets following in vitro expansion, although exendin 3 is more effective in glucose responsive cultures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the differentiated function of expanded PHHI-derived islets can be maintained by the addition of exendin 1-39 and that this may have potential for future cell replacement therapies.
low serum media and exendin-4 can extend the differentiated characteristics of PHHI cells, but only in those cultures with residual glucose responsiveness.
the endocrine characteristics of PHHI-derived cells can be maintained in culture by using low serum conditions, and in some cases exendin 1 can further enhance the endocrine characteristics.
